references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew's Sermon on the Mount: 'For all such things the Gentiles seek. But your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things' ([ref:Matt 6:32|Matthew 6:32]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:30, with almost identical wording stating that the Gentiles chase after material things and that the Father knows what we need.
Jesus emphasizes that 'your Father knows what you need before you ask him' ([ref:Matt 6:8|Matthew 6:8]). This confirms the central point in Luke 12:30 that the Father already knows our needs.

The preceding verse in context: 'Do not seek what you are to eat and what you are to drink, nor be worried' ([ref:Luk 12:29|Luke 12:29]). Luke 12:30 gives the reason for this exhortation – it is the Gentiles who chase after such things.

The following verse: 'Seek his kingdom instead, and all these things will be given to you as well' ([ref:Luk 12:31|Luke 12:31]). While verse 30 describes the Gentiles' pursuit of material things, verse 31 points to the alternative that believers should follow.

'As a father shows compassion to his children, so the Lord shows compassion to those who fear him. For he knows how we are formed; he remembers that we are dust' ([ref:Sal 103:13-14|Psalms 103:13-14]). God's fatherly care and his knowledge of our created nature support the theme in Luke 12:30 that the Father knows what we need.

Isaiah speaks of God being 'sought by those who did not ask for him … a nation that did not call on my name' ([ref:Jes 65:1|Isaiah 65:1]). The contrast between the Gentiles' search for worldly things and God's initiative toward the nations provides background for the expression 'the Gentiles of the world' (τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου) in Luke 12:30.

'Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God' ([ref:Fil 4:6|Philippians 4:6]). Paul exhorts believers not to worry, in line with Jesus' words that the Father knows our needs.

'My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus' ([ref:Fil 4:19|Philippians 4:19]). The promise that God meets the needs of believers connects directly to Jesus' assurance in Luke 12:30 that the Father knows what we need.
'Cast all your anxieties on him, because he cares for you' ([ref:1 Pet 5:7|1 Peter 5:7]). Peter's exhortation is built on the same truth as Luke 12:30: God knows our needs and cares for us.
